description: XBeach is an open source two-dimensional model of wave propagation, long (infragravity) waves, mean flow, sediment transport and morphological change on beaches, dunes and back-barrier areas during storms. It was first funded by the US Army Corps of Engineers and the US Geological Survey to assess hurricane impacts on sandy beaches, then extended by Rijkswaterstaat for dune safety assessments of Dutch flood defences and validated with EU support on beaches around European seas; it is maintained by Deltares with UNESCO-IHE, TU Delft and the University of Miami. It has a hydrostatic mode that resolves wave groups and a more demanding non-hydrostatic mode, and includes vegetation damping, hard structures, overwash, inundation, avalanching and breaching, and it has been applied to coral reefs and gravel beaches. Code is public in the Deltares Subversion repository with a GitHub mirror under the GNU Lesser GPL, a Read the Docs manual and Matlab and Python tools; Windows builds of release 1.24 need a free login. Caveats: the domain is kilometres and storm time scales, so it does not replace regional surge models, and results depend on calibrated sediment and wave settings. Simulation uses: dune and dike erosion during design storms, overwash and breaching of barrier islands, safety assessment of sandy flood defences, and sea level rise adaptation of coasts. Related records: Delft3D FM (model-delft3d-fm) provides regional surge and wave boundary conditions, and TELEMAC-MASCARET (model-telemac-mascaret) is an alternative coastal suite.
